g.text: Primate Teeth (Millions BP) & Neanderthal Cave Fires

text.tspan: • Fossilized tooth enamel demonstrates primate baseline exposure to ambient
lead going back millions of years under pristine unperturbed conditions.
• Neanderthal teeth at 250,000 BP reveal distinct episodic lead ingestion lines
from concentrated subterranean biomass smoke in enclosed cave hearths.
• Unperturbed Biological Baseline (H₀): Pre-metallurgy blood lead was
< 0.005 µg/dL — virtually non-existent compared to modern body burdens.

g.text: Çatalhöyük: The First Anthropogenic Environmental Disasters

text.tspan: • Lead's low melting point (327°C) made it the earliest metal smelted by fire,
thousands of years before copper (1085°C) or iron (1538°C) could be melted.
• First Anthropogenic Exposure: Began as catastrophic occupational poisoning
of enslaved miners and smelters, then expanded into urban settlements.
• As metallurgy activity surged, Anatolian smelters unleashed history's first
man-made atmospheric toxic plumes, inaugurating the Anthropocene.

g.text: Cheap Toxic Lead By-Product Floods Civilizations

text.tspan: • Lead was rarely mined alone; it occurred with silver (argentiferous galena).
• Extracting 1 ton of pure silver for imperial coinage required smelting
300 to 400 tons of toxic lead. Romans treated lead as 'waste to release'.
• To monetize the mountains of waste, empires engineered ubiquitous uses:
aqueduct pipes (fistulae), cistern linings, kohl cosmetics, and cookware.
• Sapa & Deflutum: Boiling sour wine in lead vats yielded sweet lead acetate
(sugar of lead), heavily consumed by Roman senators, emperors, and elite.

g.text: Boldsen et al.: Bone Concentrations in Denmark & Germany

text.tspan: "Lead exposure reached even out into the rural communities where
ca. 35% of the population was exposed above background... The
sources for Pb encompassed lead glazed ceramics in daily contact
with foodstuff; lead coins; stained glass; lead tiled roofs in contact
with drinking water... higher concentrations of Pb in urban than
in rural communities." — Boldsen, Rasmussen, et al.

g.text: "Almost Not Avoid Ingesting Lead If Wealthy or Urban"

text.tspan: "In the Middle Ages you could almost not avoid ingesting lead, if you
were wealthy or living in an urban environment... the skeletons of the
urban rich had substantially higher (and potentially toxic) levels of
lead compared to rural communities. Lead glaze was practical to clean
and looked beautiful, so it was understandably in high demand.
Lead was soft and malleable, used for coins, cups, roofs, and pipes."

g.text: Varved Sediments & Glacial Ice: Independent Pollution History

text.tspan: • Lake sediments archive the environmental legacy of preindustrial activities
across Europe, verifying historical mining independent of written records:
• Greenland Summit (Hong 1994, Rosman 1997): Clear 206Pb/207Pb isotopic shift.
• Koltjärnen & Rudegyl, Sweden (Brännvall 1997/1999): Annual varved laminae.
• Meidsee, Swiss Alps (Thevenon 2011): 40x Pb Enrichment Factor (PbEF).
• Lake Redó, Pyrenees (Camarero 1998): 500 µg/g classical Iberian peaks.
• Pandemic Plunges: Smelting collapsed during the Antonine Plague (165 CE)
and Black Death (1349 CE) as labor demand fell, confirming lead-disease ties.

g.text: NEUROPATHOLOGY: vmPFC ATROPHY ➔ IMPULSIVE WAR COMMAND
Animal Burdens Often Exceed Proximate Human Populations

text.tspan: • Flint MI Dogs (Langlois 2017): 4-fold lead surge following water crisis.
• Millie, First Dog under Bush (1990): Lead-poisoned in White House.
• Smelter Vicinity (Berny 1995): 10% humans vs >30% pets elevated.
• Cats (Knight 2003): Ingest paint dust and contaminated yard soil via paws.
• New Orleans Mockingbirds (McClelland 2019): Extreme territorial aggression
and altered vocalization matching human lead-induced prefrontal rage.
• Equal Tonnage: About equal amounts of lead were used in Lead-Based Paint
pigment (1884–1989) as in leaded gasoline (1929–1989) (~5 million tons each).
• Commuter Fallout: Suburban drivers disgorged sub-micron aerosol particles
daily into inner-city corridors, concentrating permanent toxic soil sinks.
• Housing Age Breakdown (EPA): 87% built before 1940 contains lead paint;
69% built 1940–1959; and 24% built 1960–1977 still contaminated.
• This concentrated urban loading explains the global lead-crime wave
and proves lead as the dominant 1st order physical driver of modern chaos.
